record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Dynamical Systems
record.original_question: Let M^n be a compact connected oriented manifold of dimension n ≥ 3 with Euler characteristic 0, equipped with a smooth volume form, and consider nowhere-zero divergence-free vector fields on M^n. In every homotopy class of such nowhere-zero vector fields, does there exist one whose flow has no periodic orbit?

evidence.quote: Does there exist vector fields as above (in every homotopy class of non-zero vector fields) such that the flow of fXt has no periodic orbit ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M^n$ be a compact connected oriented smooth manifold of dimension $n \ge 3$ with Euler characteristic $\chi(M) = 0$, equipped with a fixed smooth volume form $\mu$. A smooth vector field $X$ on $M$ is called divergence-free (with respect to $\mu$) if $\mathcal{L}_X \mu = 0$, equivalently if the flow generated by $X$ preserves $\mu$. Since $\chi(M)=0$, the space of nowhere-zero smooth vector fields on $M$ is nonempty, and we may consider its decomposition into homotopy classes (homotopies through nowhere-zero vector fields). Within each such homotopy class, consider those representatives that are also divergence-free with respect to $\mu$.

Prove or disprove: in every homotopy class of nowhere-zero smooth vector fields on $M^n$, there exists a representative $X$ that is divergence-free with respect to $\mu$ and whose flow has no periodic orbit.
artifact.status_search_result: In dimension 3, G. Kuperberg constructed volume-preserving aperiodic flows on every 3-manifold with Euler characteristic 0, and the plug construction does not change the homotopy type of the vector field, so on T^3 there are smooth nonsingular volume-preserving vector fields in every homotopy class with no closed orbits. However, the general statement for arbitrary compact oriented manifolds of dimension n ≥ 3 and arbitrary homotopy classes does not appear to be settled in the literature found; a definitive resolution could not be verified.

status_evidence.title: Aperiodic Dynamical Systems (Notices of the AMS)
status_evidence.snippet: G. Kuperberg modified Schweitzer's vector field to a volume-preserving counterexample to the Seifert conjecture; every 3-manifold possesses a C^1 volume-preserving flow with no fixed points and no closed trajectories.
status_evidence.claim: Volume-preserving aperiodic flows exist on every closed 3-manifold.

status_evidence.title: A volume-preserving counterexample to the Seifert conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Volume-preserving version of the Schweitzer plug.
status_evidence.claim: Kuperberg's plug preserves volume and does not alter the homotopy class of the vector field.
